newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady despite bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady despite bank lending.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Monday despite fresh injection of funds by agent banks of Bank Negara Malaysia, dealers said.
"Bank Negara agents were lending a bit of money this morning but it was not enough to pull down rates. The market is still very tight," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said although some Bank Negara agents continued lending, the market was too short to prevent a spike up in rates.
They said merchant banks and finance companies continued to bid rates up.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past 10 days to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
Dealers said rates would have gone up further but for a persistent rumour about a possible cut in banks' statutory reserves requirement (SRR).
Banks in Malaysia have to maintain a certain percentage of their deposits in liquid assets, mainly government paper.
Dealers said one-month money was at 8.5 percent against 8.4/5 percent on Friday.
Three-month money was steady at 8.3 percent.
The overnight interbank rate, which closed at 8.7/8 percent on Friday, was expected to trade around 9.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange extended their fall to reflect the firmness in interbank rates, futures dealers said.
At 0315 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down seven points to 92.25, or an implied yield of 7.75 percent.
The December contract was down five to 92.49, or 7.51 percent.
